Last Monday, my colleague and I were discussing the new grammar checker that we have been developing for two years. The feature looks quite promising, but there are still a lot of problems that need to be fixed before we can release it to users. We didn't have enough time to properly test everything because the last few weeks have been extremely busy, and everyone has other tasks to finish.
The first issues we noticed were related to spelling. For example, the application sometimes accepts misspelled words such as "receive," "separate," "definitely," "occurred," "immediately," "environment," "weird," "successful," and "until" without showing any warning. This is particularly annoying because those mistakes are very common, and a good spell checker should be able to detect them easily. It also doesn't always notice duplicated words, for example when somebody writes "the application crashed" or "we need to restart it."
Another problem is sentence capitalization. Sometimes the first word after a full stop remains lowercase. The same happens with days and months, for example Monday, January, and September. Proper names can also cause problems, especially when users write things like "I work at Microsoft" or "we visited Portugal in August." The pronoun I should obviously always be uppercase; however, right now the checker doesn't consistently correct it.
There are also several problems with subject-verb agreement. A user sometimes writes sentences such as "the feature works correctly," "the results look good," "these options are disabled," or "each of the tests has passed." The system also struggles with constructions such as "there are many errors," "there were several problems," and "there are two possible solutions."
Verb tense detection still needs improvement too. Yesterday we tested the application and found three serious bugs. Before that, we had tested an older build, and everything had worked much better. By the time the developer arrived, we had already been waiting for almost two hours. If we had tested this earlier, we could have found the problem sooner. Tomorrow we will test another version if the build is ready.
Articles are another area where the software makes many mistakes. A user can open the editor, paste text into a document, and click a button to start the review. The application should then show a list of detected issues. In some situations, it suggests incorrect phrases such as "some information," "a user," or "an apple," while in other places it completely forgets an article. For example, "I bought a new computer yesterday" requires an article before "new computer."
Plural and uncountable nouns are difficult as well. We received a lot of useful feedback from our users and important information from the testing team. One tester gave us three pieces of advice about the user interface and asked us to buy new equipment for the laboratory. We also need to review all the data collected during previous tests and decide which criteria should be used.
Prepositions often cause subtle issues. She has been working here for three years, while I have worked here since 2021. We discussed the problem during the meeting and agreed to investigate it later. He is responsible for testing the Windows version, and I am interested in checking the Linux build. We arrived at the office at 9:00 and waited for the manager for nearly 30 minutes.
Comparatives and superlatives should be tested carefully too. The new version is faster than the previous one, but it is also much simpler to use. This algorithm is the easiest solution we have tried so far. My laptop is more powerful than yours, although your computer performs well in some benchmarks. Of the two implementations, the second one is better because it uses less memory.
Pronouns can be tricky. He and I reviewed the pull request yesterday. The manager asked Sarah and me to prepare a report, then he gave the task to me. Every developer should update their own documentation when they finish a feature. Between you and me, this solution doesn't seem very reliable. The company changed its policy, but it's unclear whether the change will affect us.
Negations should also be checked. We don't need any additional tests because nobody reported any new issues. I can hardly understand why the build never finishes. The developer said that he didn't do anything wrong, but the logs showed several errors. We decided not to change anything until somebody complains.
Punctuation is probably one of the hardest areas; however, the checker should still catch obvious problems. The application works well; however, it sometimes crashes after startup. We tested Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and Safari, but only Chrome worked correctly. My colleague said, "This should work," but I wasn't convinced. If the build succeeds, we will deploy it; otherwise, we will roll back the changes. The test finished successfully; unfortunately, nobody saved the results.
Spacing and formatting should be tested as well. For example, users may type 10 kg, 25 km, 100 ms, 5 GB, or 20% CPU usage. They might also accidentally put spaces before punctuation, like this, or forget spaces after commas, like this. Sometimes they use double spaces between words or leave a space before a period. Parentheses can be wrong too, especially when spaces are missing.
Numbers and dates create additional edge cases. On September 5th, 2026, we performed three different tests using two machines. The first machine had 16 GB of RAM, and the second had 32 GB. Test number one took 1.5 seconds, while another took 0.75 seconds. We measured a 20 percent improvement, but CPU utilization increased by 5 percent. The experiment was repeated on September 21st and October 3rd.
Word choice is another important category. The new configuration had a big effect on performance, but it did not affect stability. We should ensure that every setting is saved correctly. The new interface is very intuitive, except for the advanced settings page. They're going to update the documentation later, but I don't know whether they will finish it today. The developer whose laptop crashed said that the problem was caused by a loose cable.
Some sentences are grammatical but still sound unnatural. Please revert the changes when you are finished. We need to collaborate to improve the final outcome. The reason is that the server was overloaded. We are currently testing the newest version. Each developer should review their own changes. In my opinion, the interface is too complicated.
Conditional sentences also cause trouble. If I find another bug, I will report it. If I had known about the issue yesterday, I would have fixed it. If the server hadn't crashed, the test would have finished successfully. Unless you restart the application, the changes won't be applied. I wish the program worked more reliably.
Questions and indirect questions are another useful test. Do you know where the configuration file is? Can you tell me why the process crashed? I wonder what this option does. The manager asked whether we had finished the test. Nobody knows when the new version will be released.
There are also mistakes involving infinitives and gerunds. I enjoy working on difficult technical problems, but I avoid working late at night. The application allows users to edit their text and helps them find mistakes. We decided to test the feature again tomorrow and suggested adding more unit tests. She made me restart the service and let me check the logs.
Finally, the checker should deal with sentences that contain several mistakes at once. Yesterday, John and I were working on a feature that doesn't work properly, and we were trying to understand why it crashes every few minutes. After nearly two hours, we finally found the problem: there were too many threads running at the same time, and each of them was consuming more memory than it should have. We fixed the bug, ran the tests again, and everything seemed to work well, but nobody has checked whether the solution actually solves the original issue yet.
